subject: Future Tech
title: Growing Food Off Earth
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Growing Food Off Earth.

hook.text: Shipping food from Earth costs $20,000 per kilogram. Colonists must grow their own or starve.

buildup.text: Astronauts on the ISS grew lettuce under LED lights in 2015. It was the first food eaten that was grown in orbit.

discovery.text: Hydroponics and aeroponics use up to 90% less water than soil farming, critical when every drop is precious.

twist.text: Plants need more than light and water.

climax.text: NASA's Veggie and APH experiments are testing dozens of crops. Tomatoes, peppers, and radishes all grew in orbit.

punchline.text: The first Martian farmer will grow dinner under LEDs.

quiz.question: How much less water does hydroponics use compared to soil farming?
